sources.title: Interfering with employee rights (Section 7 and 8(a)(1))
sources.scope: Private-sector Section 7 and 8(a)(1) rights and employer-interference examples.
limits: Coverage and protected-status questions remain fact-specific.

sources.title: Concerted Activity
sources.scope: Examples of protected collective action, including safety complaints and group workplace concerns.
limits: Does not classify conduct in any named Wave 04 case.

sources.title: Protected Concerted Activity
sources.scope: Public examples of complaints, settlements, reinstatement, backpay and record correction following protected concerted activity.
limits: Each example retains its own procedural posture; settlement is not a universal merits ruling.

sources.title: Weingarten Rights
sources.scope: Right of union-represented employees, upon request, to representation in covered investigatory interviews.
limits: Current Board-law scope is not generalized to every worker or meeting.

sources.title: Employee right to report injuries and illnesses free from retaliation
sources.scope: Reporting rights and examples of adverse action, including points that can lead to future consequences.
limits: Claim-specific causation and filing rules remain outside this wave.

sources.title: Safety Management - Worker Participation
sources.scope: Worker and union-representative participation, access to safety information, and removal of reporting barriers.
limits: Recommended-practice guidance is not a complete adjudication standard.

sources.title: Frequently Asked Questions on Warehouse Quotas (Assembly Bill 701)
sources.scope: Quota disclosure, personal work-speed data, break and safety boundaries, complaints and retaliation presumption.

sources.title: Warehouse Worker Protection Act
sources.publisher: New York State Department of Labor
sources.scope: Quota and work-speed disclosure, breaks, injury-reduction program and anti-retaliation rights.
limits: Covered New York warehouse scope only.
